adjudication.scale_caveat_recorded_at_his_instruction: the token interface is 29.2% of THIS parent and ~1% of a 70B model by the same arithmetic (docs/PHASE1 section 4.1); these rows are this model's phase-1 numbers, not a transferable strategy

axes.selection: one shared orthonormal basis E (1024 x 896), the top eigenvectors of the reader-pca second moment of the residual stream pooled over all 29 residual-write endpoints with each endpoint equalised to trace one; a per-boundary chart is not expressible in a stock child because the residual is a running sum with nowhere to put a chart transition.  The conv blocks' internal channels are a pivoted-Cholesky coreset of the parent's own, because Lfm2ShortConv gates channelwise and no rotation of that space is representable
axes.solve: readers folded EXACTLY as sqrt(1024/H) W diag(g) E diag(1/g_c) with g_c = diag(E^T diag(g) E) (the lift preserves the norm, so the parent's RMSNorm at the lifted row and the child's at the row differ by that one constant); writers folded as E^T W and re-solved against the child's own installed activations by the prior-anchored ridge under THE LAW; the final norm's diagonal solved in closed form against the tied head's Gram
axes.evidence: sequentially conditioned capture through the partially built child

axes.selection: pivoted-Cholesky coreset of real channels, ranked on the CHILD's OWN gated intermediate captured through the live narrowed body -- the MLP counterpart of the conv coreset's `parent_gated_rows`, and equal to the parent's gated intermediate at the lifted row up to bf16 because the reader fold is exact there; w1/w3 rows kept verbatim from the FOLDED readers, which is the same object as folding the parent's kept rows because the basis and the coreset commute
axes.solve: prior-anchored ridge on the folded w2 restricted to the kept columns, lambda ladder to update_scale<=1.0, arm=conditioned-local
axes.evidence: sequentially conditioned capture through the partially built child: block i's census sees every narrowing above it

axes.selection: the 12288 rows kept by: every added/special token and every one of the 256 ByteLevel alphabet tokens (mandatory -- byte_fallback is false and there is no unk, so those 256 are the only reason an arbitrary byte can still be encoded), the transitive merge-tree closure of everything kept, and then the ranking (-census count, parent token id) until the budget is exactly met.  The census sums two streams over the sealed corpus: the donor-mapped ids the captures ran on and this tokenizer's own canonical segmentation of the same text.  With only 4633 observed tokens admitted beyond the mandatory set, the tie-break -- parent id order, which for a BPE table is its merge order and therefore its training-corpus frequency order -- decides most of this table, and that is stated rather than implied
axes.solve: NONE.  The rows are gathered verbatim; the identity gate is torch.equal against the source table's own bytes, not a tolerance.  The merge list is restricted to the closure (a merge survives iff its product and both operands are kept) and the ids are densely remapped, including the TemplateProcessing special-token ids, which carry hard ids a remap that missed them would silently corrupt
axes.evidence: the sealed corpus, for a token OCCURRENCE census only; no activation, no capture, no forward pass
axes.heldout: not applicable: nothing is fitted.  What IS measured out of sample is the segmentation shift -- position agreement 1.0000 on the sealed corpus and 0.0992 on the frozen review prompts, with tokens-per-byte beside it

vocabulary.mandatory_rule: all 509 added/special tokens, all 256 ByteLevel alphabet tokens, and the transitive merge-tree closure of both
vocabulary.sealed_corpus_is_a_donor_mapped_stream: mapped_donor_calibration.json carries a DONOR tokenizer's segmentation mapped into this vocabulary, so the parent does not round-trip its own sealed corpus (264 donor ids re-encode to 186 canonical ones on row 0).  The census therefore reads BOTH streams and both coverages are published.

kept_token_occurrences_lost.claim: every token occurrence in the sealed corpus, on both streams, has a kept row; asserted, not asserted-about

lossless_on_text_and_agreement.claim: decode(child_encode(t)) == t for every t (the byte alphabet is complete and there is no unk); `position_agreement` is how often the child's segmentation equals the parent's under the remap, and it is the measured size of the input-distribution shift this arm bets on

evidence.split_authority: not consumed: the base arm solves nothing
